title: Heightfield terrain with skirts and surface queries
purpose: Turn a row-major array of heights into a three.js terrain mesh with exact central-difference normals, UVs, an LOD stride, skirts that hide gaps between tiles and an optional bottom that closes a diorama block, plus bilinear and on-mesh height queries for placing objects. Use it for terrain tiles, maps and dioramas.

engine.name: webgl2_browser
engine.notes: heightfieldTerrainData, sampleHeight and sampleSurfaceHeight need no three.js; createHeightfieldTerrainGeometry takes three.js as THREE; only 0.186.1 was run.

exports.name: heightfieldTerrainData
exports.signature: heightfieldTerrainData(heights, width, depth, options = {}) -> {positions, normals, uvs, indices, columns, rows}
exports.summary: The terrain grid as typed arrays, with optional skirts and bottom.

exports.name: createHeightfieldTerrainGeometry
exports.signature: createHeightfieldTerrainGeometry(THREE, heights, width, depth, options = {}) -> THREE.BufferGeometry
exports.summary: The same data in a BufferGeometry with an index and computed bounds.

exports.name: sampleHeight
exports.signature: sampleHeight(heights, width, depth, x, z) -> number
exports.summary: Bilinear height at sample coordinates, clamped to the field.

exports.name: sampleSurfaceHeight
exports.signature: sampleSurfaceHeight(heights, width, depth, x, z) -> number
exports.summary: Height on the mesh triangles themselves (stride 1).

inputs.heights: array or typed array of width * depth finite numbers, row-major: index = z * width + x

options.name: stride
options.meaning: Use every stride-th sample (LOD); it must divide width - 1 and depth - 1.

options.name: skirt
options.meaning: Add four outward walls down to the base height.

options.name: skirtBase
options.meaning: World y of the skirt bottom; null is one cell size under the lowest point; it may not be above the lowest point.

options.name: closeBottom
options.meaning: Add a bottom facing down so the block is closed (needs skirt).

options.name: center
options.meaning: Centre the grid on the origin; otherwise sample (0, 0) is at the origin.

limits: A regular grid with one fixed diagonal per cell: no adaptive triangulation, no overhangs, caves or vertical cliffs, and the diagonal direction can show on steep ridges. Normals come from the full-resolution field even at a coarser stride, so lighting stays steady across LOD levels but does not match the coarse triangles exactly. Skirts hide cracks between tiles of different strides; they do not stitch them. sampleHeight is bilinear and differs from the mesh inside non-planar cells; sampleSurfaceHeight matches the mesh at stride 1 only. Grids above 65,535 vertices use 32-bit indices. Only three.js 0.186.1 was run, in headless Chrome on SwiftShader WebGL 2.
technique_references: Central-difference normals (-dh/dx, 1, -dh/dz) with one-sided differences at the borders
Barycentric interpolation on the mesh's triangle split
Skirt walls for level-of-detail terrain tiles
